title: Intrinsic randomness generation explains most randomness in nature

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Intrinsic randomness generation explains most randomness in nature

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The mechanism in which a system's own deterministic rules generate randomness without any random input is ultimately responsible for a large fraction, and perhaps essentially all, of the randomness seen in the natural world.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 7: Mechanisms in Programs and Nature

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: I believe that this mechanism is in fact ultimately responsible for a large fraction, if not essentially all, of the randomness that we see in the natural world.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 7, “Mechanisms in Programs and Nature”; section “Randomness from the Environment” (from p. 301), p. 301. Scope: random-looking phenomena in the natural world

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch07-03: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.32

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim has empirical implications once a population and attribution method are fixed. Existing datasets cover selected phenomena, not the near-universal natural scope, and generally lack interventions needed to separate mechanisms.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define a representative inventory of natural random-looking phenomena and, for each, estimate the fraction of unpredictability attributable to deterministic internal dynamics versus environmental and initial-condition uncertainty. Weight the inventory by a prespecified measure to test whether the intrinsic fraction is large or nearly total.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No representative census of randomness in nature exists.

“Large fraction” has no weighting measure.

Mechanisms are often observationally non-identifiable.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.12
analysis feasibility: 0.22
discriminating power: 0.28
data existence: 0.58
operationalizability: 0.3

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The later repeatability criterion makes the mechanism assignment measurable in principle, so the sentence is not empty. Public archives do not contain that assignment for any representative catalogue of natural randomness, and the text itself treats the attribution as a belief to be illustrated later. Settling a large fraction, let alone essentially all, requires data that have not been collected for this purpose.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For each phenomenon in a declared catalogue of natural randomness, use repeatability under controlled perturbations to assign intrinsic generation, environmental input, or initial-condition transcription, then compute the fraction assigned to intrinsic generation. A small fraction would refute a large fraction, if not essentially all.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Most observational records remain compatible with environmental or initial-condition accounts.

Mechanism labels require repeated, perturbation-controlled runs that were usually not archived.

The scope is a large fraction of randomness in the natural world, far beyond any existing catalogue.

data existence: 0.3

operationalizability: 0.55
analysis feasibility: 0.25
